title: Real-time chat v2: project chat terminology, live project-channel membership, rich code and attachment rendering, and channel members

overview.problemStatement: Chat v1 works, but it describes itself as team chat while the product is organised around projects. A person assigned a task joins the project yet their open chat does not learn about the project channel until a reload, and messages that arrive over the socket can render the author as 'Unknown member' because not every socket payload carries a populated author. Code pasted into the composer is shown as prose, images are shown as a filename link, and every attachment link points at a protected API route that the browser opens without an Authorization header, so viewing a file answers 'Not authorized, no token'. The chat header's member-count control calls an empty handler, and the project detail page offers no way into the project's conversation.
overview.proposedSolution: A backwards-compatible second pass over the chat module. The seeded team channel becomes 'Project Chat', the conversation segment becomes 'Project channels' and all team-channel copy becomes project-channel copy while the stored kind stays 'team'. A task assignment that adds a person to a project emits the project channel card to that person's user room and the client appends it and joins its room, with project renames refreshing the card the same way. Pasted code becomes a fenced block with an inferred language and renders as a code card with a language label, syntax colours, Copy and Download. Images render as thumbnails that open in an in-app lightbox and other files as file cards that download, all fetched as blobs through the authenticated axios client so no protected URL is ever navigated to. The project detail header gains an 'Open chat' action backed by a get-or-create project-channel endpoint. Every message payload carries a populated author with a client-side directory fallback, and the header member control opens a WhatsApp-style panel listing the channel's members with presence, workspace role and a 'You' badge.
overview.targetAudience: Workspace members who read or write chat (Developer, Team Member, Scrum Master, Product Owner, Administrator) and the project members who gain a channel through task assignment. No new role or permission is introduced.
assumptions: Team chat means the seeded workspace-wide channel named 'Team Chat'; team channel means the per-project channel currently labelled 'Team channels'. Both are display and data changes, not a new channel type.
The project detail header action is an in-app navigation, not a new tab; the chat screen already supports deep links to /{workspaceSlug}/chat/{channelId}.
A member's workspace role (Workspace.members[].roleId) is the role shown in the member panel; projects have no role of their own, so no project-level admin/member distinction is invented.
Their details means avatar, display name, online state and workspace role. Email addresses are deliberately not exposed to every channel reader.
Attachment previews render the original file; no thumbnail pipeline or image re-encoding is added.
Socket.IO remains the only live channel; the existing REST fallback and 10-second activity poll are unchanged.
outOfScope: Changing chat permissions, the channel kind enum, or the v1 access rules.
Replacing Socket.IO, adding a second realtime transport, or changing the Vercel serverless entry that cannot host a socket.
Voice and video, message translation, AI summarisation, bots or inbound webhooks.
Per-project roles, project-level chat moderation, or a second membership model.
Server-side image thumbnailing, transcoding or virus scanning beyond the existing upload MIME allow-list.
Rebuilding the composer as a rich-text editor; pasted code is still stored as message text with fences.
Merging or rebasing feature/chat onto the current main (recorded as RISK-007, not performed by this feature).

userStories.title: The chat surface speaks about projects
userStories.want: the chat surface to say project chat and project channel
userStories.benefit: the vocabulary matches the projects the conversation belongs to

acceptanceCriteria.text: In every workspace, the seeded team channel displays as 'Project Chat' in the sidebar, the chat header, search results and conversation previews; an existing workspace is migrated by an idempotent backfill rather than a manual step.
The chat screen's channel section is titled 'Project channels', its empty and footer copy says 'project channel', and no user-facing string in the chat surface says 'Team Chat' or 'team channel'.
The API still returns kind 'team' for that channel, so stored rows, permissions, indexes and access rules are unchanged.

userStories.title: A new assignee gets the project channel live
userStories.role: Assignee newly added to a task
userStories.want: the project's channel to appear in my chat without reloading
userStories.benefit: I can join the conversation the assignment just gave me access to

acceptanceCriteria.text: Assigning a workspace member to a task in a project adds them to that project's members and ensures the project has a channel.
The newly added assignee's open chat screen gains the project's channel row, showing the project's current name, within 2 seconds and without a page reload.
The new row carries the channel id and member count, and the assignee's socket joins that channel's room so the next message in it arrives live.
A member who was already on the project receives no duplicate row and no event, and a bulk edit emits at most one channel event per project and user pair.

userStories.title: Pasted code is shown as code
userStories.want: a pasted snippet to appear as a code block with its language and actions
userStories.benefit: the message is readable and reusable

acceptanceCriteria.text: Pasting multi-line code into the composer inserts it as a fenced block with the inferred language and preserves indentation.
A message whose body is fenced code, or is clearly code without fences, renders a code card with a language label, syntax colours, Copy and Download.
Copy writes the raw code without the fences to the clipboard and announces success; Download saves the snippet with an extension derived from the language.
A snippet that is too large or of unknown language still renders readably - labelled 'text', no colour assumptions - and is never interpreted as HTML.

userStories.title: Attachments show what they are and open without an error
userStories.want: to see the image or a file card and open it inside the app
userStories.benefit: I do not hit an authentication error

acceptanceCriteria.text: An image attachment renders as a thumbnail in the message; a non-image attachment renders as a file card with its name, size and a type icon.
Clicking an image opens an in-app lightbox with the full image; clicking a file downloads it. Neither action navigates the browser to a protected API URL.
Attachments are loaded through the authenticated API client, so a fresh load of a message with an attachment never renders 'Not authorized, no token'.
Object URLs are cached per attachment and revoked when no longer used, so paging or re-rendering does not refetch the same file and does not leak unbounded memory.
The composer previews pending attachments as image thumbnails or file cards before sending, and removing a pending attachment still works.

userStories.title: Reach the project chat from the project
userStories.role: Project member reading the project detail page
userStories.want: a chat action in the header
userStories.benefit: I can move from the project's work to its conversation in one click

acceptanceCriteria.text: The project detail header shows an 'Open chat' action beside Edit, Open board and New sprint for users who can read chat.
The action opens that project's channel, resolving it on demand if it does not exist yet, and is hidden from a user without chat:read.

userStories.title: A live message always names its author
userStories.want: the author's name and avatar immediately
userStories.benefit: a new message is never anonymous

acceptanceCriteria.text: A message received over the socket displays the author's name and avatar immediately, with no refresh.

An edit, pin or unpin broadcast also carries the author, and a payload that carries only an author id is resolved against the member directory, so 'Unknown member' is never shown for a known participant.

userStories.title: See who is in the channel
userStories.want: the member control to open a list of everyone in the channel with their details
userStories.benefit: I know who I am talking to

acceptanceCriteria.text: Clicking the members control in the chat header opens a member panel; the control no longer has an empty handler.
The panel lists each member with avatar, name, online state, workspace role and a 'You' badge, online members first, and its member count matches the number on the header.
A project channel lists the project's members, the two default channels list workspace members, and a direct conversation lists its two participants.
The panel is keyboard operable - it opens with focus inside, closes on Escape and returns focus to the trigger - and at 320px it fits without horizontal scrolling.

functionalRequirements.text: The seeded team channel MUST be stored and returned as 'Project Chat'; the existing-workspace backfill MUST rename a channel named 'Team Chat' idempotently and MUST NOT create a second default channel.
Every user-facing chat string MUST read 'Project Chat' / 'project channel' / 'Project channels'; the internal kind value MUST remain 'team'.
The chat screen's channel section MUST be titled 'Project channels' and its footer MUST state that only project members can read a project channel.
A create or update that changes a task's assignees MUST keep adding the new assignees to the task's project and MUST ensure that project's channel exists before any event is emitted.

The server MUST emit a chat:channel-granted event to the user room of each assignee newly added to a project, carrying the channel card: id, name, project id, avatar URL, member count and archived flag.
The client MUST append a granted channel to the Project channels list, deduplicate by id, refresh ordering, and join its socket room without a reload.
The server MUST NOT emit chat:channel-granted for an assignee who was already a project member, and MUST collapse a bulk change to one event per project and user pair.
When a project is renamed, the server MUST emit the updated channel summary so open chat screens show the new project name.

The composer MUST detect a pasted multi-line code snippet and insert it as a fenced block tagged with an inferred language, preserving the pasted indentation and not double-wrapping text that is already fenced.
The message renderer MUST render fenced code and clearly-code bodies as a code card with a language label, syntax highlighting, Copy and Download.
Copy MUST copy the raw code without fences; Download MUST save it with an extension derived from the language; both MUST work without the message being editable.
Snippet detection, language inference and download naming MUST be pure functions in client/src/features/chat/lib/ covered by unit tests (CON-202).

The message renderer MUST show image attachments as thumbnails and non-image attachments as file cards with name, size and a type icon, while keeping the attachment name available to assistive technology.
Activating an image attachment MUST open an in-app lightbox; activating a file attachment MUST download the file. Neither action may navigate the browser to the API route.
Attachment bytes MUST be fetched with the authenticated API client as blobs; the chat surface MUST NOT place an auth token in a URL, query string or anchor href.
Loaded attachment object URLs MUST be cached per attachment id and revoked when the last consumer unmounts.
The composer's pending-attachment list MUST preview images as thumbnails and other files as cards, and MUST keep the existing remove control.
The project detail header MUST render an 'Open chat' action for callers with chat:read that links to that project's channel.
The API MUST expose the channel for one project, get-or-create semantics included, so the project header can link directly without loading every conversation.
Every socket payload that carries a message MUST carry a populated author (name and avatar), including chat:message, chat:updated and the REST responses they mirror.
The client MUST resolve an author id against the channel member directory when a message payload carries only an id, and MUST NOT render 'Unknown member' for a known participant.
The chat header member control MUST open a member panel instead of calling an empty handler.

The API MUST expose the members of one channel - project members for a project channel, workspace members for the two default channels, and the two participants for a direct conversation - with id, name, avatar URL, workspace role name and online state.
The member panel MUST show avatar, name, online state, role and a 'You' badge, group online members first, and state a count equal to the header's member count.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: A project channel granted by a task assignment MUST be visible on an already-open chat screen within 2 seconds p95 on a normal connection, or on the next load if the assignee is offline; no polling interval may be added to achieve it.
The channel-members endpoint MUST resolve the list in at most two database queries and MUST NOT query once per member.
Attachment object URLs MUST be shared per attachment id for the life of the message list, so the same file is fetched once, and MUST be revoked when the last consumer unmounts.
Syntax highlighting MUST be lazy-loaded on the client and MUST NOT delay first paint or typing; a code block above 20,000 characters MUST fall back to plain monospace text.
The code card, lightbox and member panel MUST be keyboard operable, expose accessible names, trap focus where they are modal, close on Escape and restore focus to the trigger (CON-305).
The lightbox and the member panel MUST be usable at 320px without horizontal scrolling, and the code card MUST scroll its own horizontal overflow rather than widening the conversation (CON-306).

Every new route MUST run protect then requirePermission('chat:read') and MUST resolve the channel through the existing loadChannelForCaller rules, so project membership is enforced exactly as in v1 (CON-511, CON-512).
Every new path parameter MUST be validated as an ObjectId and every query MUST filter by req.workspace._id; no user input may be interpolated into a query (CON-515, CON-516).
Code and message bodies MUST be rendered as React text nodes; dangerouslySetInnerHTML MUST NOT be introduced (CON-517).
The new routes MUST inherit the application Helmet headers and the general API rate limiter; no new bypass or direct process.env read may be added (CON-513, CON-514, CON-206, CON-519).
Attachment access MUST keep using the bearer token over HTTPS and MUST NOT introduce a token in a URL, a long-lived public link or a new storage service (CON-520).
The upload MIME allow-list and filename sanitisation MUST remain the only content gate; the stored type MAY be used for rendering decisions but MUST NOT be trusted as proof of content (CON-507).
A failed attachment fetch, a failed code highlight and a failed member query MUST each degrade to a readable fallback without unhandled rejections or console errors.

edgeCases.description: An assignment lands on a project whose channel does not exist yet.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The channel is created first, then the card is emitted.

edgeCases.description: The assignee is already a project member.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: No event and no duplicate row; their existing card stays.
No event is stored; the channel appears on their next conversations load and no stale notification is replayed.

edgeCases.description: The same task is edited twice in a bulk operation.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: At most one chat:channel-granted per project and user.

edgeCases.description: Pasted text already contains a fence.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: It is sent as-is rather than double-wrapped.

edgeCases.description: Pasted text is prose with a single line break.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: It stays prose; detection requires code signals, not just a newline.

edgeCases.description: A code block exceeds the highlight limit.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Plain monospace with Copy and Download still available.

edgeCases.description: An attachment fetch fails (expired session, file removed).
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The message shows a retryable placeholder with the name, never a broken image or an auth error page.

edgeCases.description: The channel is a direct conversation.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The panel lists exactly the two participants and the header count stays 2.

edgeCases.description: A presence event is missed while the panel is open.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The member shows as offline until the next event; no invented last-seen time.

edgeCases.description: A user without chat:read opens a project page.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The Open chat action is absent and no channel request is made.

edgeCases.description: The project is archived or the channel is read-only.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The granted card shows the archived treatment and posting stays disabled.

edgeCases.description: A project is renamed while a member has the chat open.
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The row and header update to the new name without a reload.

dependencies.name: prism-react-renderer
dependencies.notes: New client dependency for token-based syntax highlighting without a stylesheet; lazy-loaded by the code card. Skill expected before implementation.

dependencies.name: axios
dependencies.notes: Reused for authenticated blob fetches of attachments.

dependencies.name: socket.io
dependencies.notes: Reused server and client; one new event on the existing user room.

dependencies.name: lucide-react
dependencies.notes: Reused icon set for message, file, image and download actions.

risks.description: feature/chat is about 100 commits behind main and 20 ahead, so merging into main will conflict in the chat files.
risks.mitigation: Keep v2 changes inside the files this spec names and treat the rebase/merge of main as a separate reviewed step.

risks.description: A syntax highlighter can add bundle weight.
risks.mitigation: Lazy import, a single small language set and the 20,000-character cap.

risks.description: Caching image blobs can grow memory in a long session.
risks.mitigation: One cache entry per attachment id, revoked on last unmount, and only the rendered page is fetched.

risks.description: A bulk assignment could emit many channel events.
risks.mitigation: Diff the member list and collapse events by project and user.

risks.description: Renaming the stored channel can collide with an existing 'Project Chat' row under the unique workspace/kind/nameKey index.
risks.mitigation: Rename only when no team row already holds the target name; otherwise leave the existing row untouched.

risks.description: Changing the message renderer can regress the v1 search jump, pin panel or thread panel.
risks.mitigation: Keep the body renderer a child component and preserve the data-message-id contract used by search.
